# Introduction

This guide takes a local DRAGEN or Rastair file from header inspection to
a regional query. It shows how to choose a sample and interpret measurements
when the callers use different allele or CpG context slots.

# Installation

For the development version, follow the [installation instructions][install].
Once methylVCF is available on Bioconductor, install it with its tutorial
dependencies.

```{r installation, eval=FALSE}
BiocManager::install("methylVCF", dependencies = TRUE)
```

# Inspect the file

Use `inspectMethylVcf()` before choosing a region. It reports the caller,
samples, contigs and declared methylation fields from the header. The
function recognizes DRAGEN and Rastair from their header declarations.
Supply `format = "dragen"` or `format = "rastair"` if the caller cannot be
identified.

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(methylVCF)
```

```{r inspect}
dragen_file <- system.file("extdata", "dragen-multisample.g.vcf", package = "methylVCF")
info <- inspectMethylVcf(dragen_file)
info
info$samples
```

The printed summary is a quick overview. Use `info$seqinfo` to get the
declared contigs, lengths and assemblies, `info$fields` for the field
declarations and `info$checks` for the header checks.

By default, the inspector tries to open the index it finds.
`info$index$status` distinguishes `"absent"`, `"readable"` and
`"unreadable"`. With `check_index = FALSE`, a sidecar found on disk is
reported as `"detected"`. The bundled gVCF has no index. When both sidecars
are present, CSI takes precedence even if it is unreadable. A readable
index can still belong to a different file. Use the matching sidecar when
you query. The inspection reads only the header and optionally opens the
index.

# Set up a regional query

Choose a local file, an interval on the VCF's reference assembly, and
the caller's format. Use the contig name as it appears in the header
(for example, `chr21` or `21`). The region uses 1-based inclusive
coordinates. By default the reader returns all samples. Use `samples`
to request specific VCF sample IDs.

Pass `info$format` to `readMethylVcf()` after identifying the caller. If
`info$format` is `NA`, supply the known format to `inspectMethylVcf()` first.
Omitting `format` from `readMethylVcf()` selects DRAGEN.

```{r regional-query}
region <-
    tibble::tibble(seqnames = "chr21", start = 13204474L, end = 13204520L) |>
    plyranges::as_granges()

calls <- readMethylVcf(
    dragen_file, region, format = info$format, samples = info$samples[[1L]]
)
as.data.frame(calls)[c("start", "sample", "scope", "fraction")]
```

For indexed access, place the matching index beside the BGZF file, for example
`sample.g.vcf.gz.tbi`. CSI (`.csi`) is also supported and takes
precedence if both indices exist. Plain text and unindexed gzip inputs
are scanned sequentially. Check the chosen path in
`S4Vectors::metadata(calls)$access` (`"tabix"` or `"sequential"`).

# Read a phased DRAGEN variant

To read a variant, ask for its coordinate just as you would for a
reference site. The example below includes both orders of a phased
heterozygous genotype.

```{r dragen}
variant <-
    tibble::tibble(seqnames = "chr21", start = 13204520L, width = 1L) |>
    plyranges::as_granges()

calls <- readMethylVcf(dragen_file, variant, format = info$format)
calls |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::select(
        sample,
        genotype,
        allele_index,
        haplotype,
        phase_set,
        fraction,
        informative_depth
    )
```

In `sample_a`, `1|0` puts ALT first, so fraction 0.8 is assigned to ALT
and fraction 0 to REF. In `sample_b`, `0|1` puts REF first. Read
`allele_index` as 0 for REF, 1 for the first ALT, and so on. Read
`haplotype` as the slot in the phased genotype. It is meaningful within a
sample, contig and phase set. A pooled call has no per-copy assignment.
[DRAGEN methylation fields][dragen]

# Read a Rastair CpG context

Rastair indicates whether a call comes from a reference CpG (`CPG`)
or a newly formed CpG (`CPGnovo`). The bundled example follows the
2.3.0-rc1 layout with separate slots for the reported contexts.

```{r rastair}
file <- system.file("extdata", "rastair-example.vcf", package = "methylVCF")
info <- inspectMethylVcf(file)
region <-
    tibble::tibble(seqnames = "chr19", start = 6105744L, end = 6105760L) |>
    plyranges::as_granges()

calls <- readMethylVcf(file, region, format = info$format)
calls |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::select(
        start,
        strand,
        motif_origin,
        allele_index,
        fraction,
        informative_depth
    )
```

At 6,105,750 the two contexts have distinct slots. At 6,105,760 a reported
de novo context could be anchored to multiple local alleles. The fraction
and depth remain available, with an unspecified strand and allele index.
This layout encodes context and local allele information.
[Rastair VCF format][rastair]

# Diagnose an incomplete import

Use the default `on_problem = "error"` for strict import. To inspect what
can be recovered, use `on_problem = "report"` and read the diagnostics.
File, header and index errors still stop either mode.
For Rastair, a slot with `ADM5mC` greater than `DPM5mC` is invalid. Report
mode records the affected slot and retains valid measurements.

Rastair 2.2.0 can report one slot for a record carrying both CpG flags.
The package includes an example generated by Rastair on artificial reads.
The following query returns the readable rows and warns about the
unsupported record at position 302.

```{r diagnostics}
file <- system.file("extdata", "rastair-2.2.0-synthetic.vcf", package = "methylVCF")
region <-
    tibble::tibble(seqnames = "synthetic", start = 300L, end = 320L) |>
    plyranges::as_granges()

calls <- readMethylVcf(file, region, format = "rastair", on_problem = "report")
calls |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::select(start, motif_origin, fraction, informative_depth)

S4Vectors::metadata(calls)$diagnostics |>
    tibble::as_tibble() |>
    dplyr::select(pos, type, reason)
```

For caller versions, fixture provenance and comparisons with raw records,
see the [validation report][validation]. Rastair software attribution
is Copyright © 2025, University of Oxford. For aligned reference
measurements, see the [regional workflow](methylVCF.html).
